_note: Hand-written scene for each card, true to the myth, keyed by card id. build_manifest.py uses it in place of the automatic subject line. Edit a line, re-run build_manifest.py, then regenerate that card with --ids <id> --force.

ody.spear: A seasoned Ithacan spearman, a grown soldier in a simple bronze helmet and linen cuirass, braced behind a round bronze shield, spear levelled, on the rocky shore of Ithaca with a dark sea behind him at dusk.
ody.sailor: A sailor of Odysseus's fleet straining at the oar of a black-hulled Greek ship with painted eyes on its prow, spray flying, the wine-dark sea at dusk.
ody.spearc: A bronze-tipped spear hurled across the plain of Troy in a duel before the city walls, caught mid-flight, dust and a blood-red setting sun behind it.
ody.aegis: Athena's aegis, the goatskin cloak fringed with golden serpents and bearing the Gorgon's head, spread in divine light over a kneeling Greek warrior.
ody.camp: A ragged camp follower in the Greek camp on the beach at Troy, carrying a basket and a water jar between the beached black ships and smoking cook-fires.
ody.sent: An Argive sentinel on night watch on the earthen wall the Greeks built to guard their ships at Troy, a tall shield planted beside him, watch-fires behind.
ody.hopl: An Argive warrior behind a towering Mycenaean figure-of-eight body shield, wearing a boar's-tusk helmet as Homer describes, braced and immovable on the plain of Troy.
ody.gate: A guard standing before the Lion Gate of Mycenae, two carved lionesses above the massive stone lintel, his spear barring the way, torchlight on the stone.
ody.ajax: Ajax the Great, giant of the Greeks, behind his tower shield of seven ox-hides faced with bronze, holding the line alone at the Greek ships as Trojan torches come at him.
ody.rampart: The towering walls of Troy, which the myths say Poseidon and Apollo built, seen from below at dusk, torches burning along the battlements.
ody.doct: A disciplined phalanx seen head-on: rows of round bronze shields locked rim to rim, spears levelled, crested helmets, dust rising around them.
ody.hearth: The great hearth of Odysseus's hall on Ithaca, the fire burning low; in the shadows Penelope's loom holds the burial shroud she weaves by day and unravels by night.
ody.drill: Greek soldiers drilling in formation on a dusty training ground beneath a mountain, a scarred old instructor shouting the time.
ody.wall: A wall of round aspis shields painted with bold emblems (a scorpion, a Gorgon's face, a charging bull), locked together, seen close up.
ody.testudo: Warriors crouched under a locked roof of shields as a rain of arrows and stones falls on them from a city wall.
ody.shield: The Shield of Achilles that the smith god Hephaestus forged, its bronze face worked in rings showing earth, sea, sky, cities at peace and at war, glowing on the anvil of his forge.
ody.thess: A Thessalian horseman galloping across the plains of Thessaly, cloak streaming, javelin raised, a storm sky over the mountains behind.
ody.zerk: A frenzied warrior possessed by Ares, eyes wild, mouth open in a war cry, charging, while the war god's red shadow looms behind him in the smoke.
ody.agam: Agamemnon, king of Mycenae and leader of the Greek host at Troy, in gold-trimmed armour, raising his ancestral sceptre to rally the army before the ships.
ody.achil: Achilles in the divine armour Hephaestus made him, leaping forward with his great ash spear, the plain and walls of Troy behind him, his one vulnerable heel just visible.
ody.fury: Ares, god of war, in a crested helmet and wreathed in red fire, gripping a mortal warrior's arm and filling him with sudden battle-rage.
ody.rally: A herald on a hilltop blowing a war horn as the scattered Greek warriors below rise and turn back toward the fight.
ody.spoils: A heap of plunder on a beach beside a black ship: bronze tripods, golden cups, captured armour and shields, glinting in torchlight.
ody.banner: A war standard on a tall pole, a crimson banner snapping in the wind over the Greek camp at Troy, the beached black ships behind.
ody.ares: The great bronze spear of Ares, god of war, standing upright in scorched earth, smoke and embers swirling around it on a ruined battlefield.
ody.ox: A white ox with gilded horns and a garland of flowers being led to the altar for sacrifice, as in the Homeric rites, smoke and a priest waiting.
ody.argus: Argus, Odysseus's old hound, lying worn and neglected by the palace gate on Ithaca, lifting his head and wagging his tail as he recognises his master, returned after twenty years disguised as a beggar.
ody.pythia: The Pythia, the oracle of Delphi, seated on a bronze tripod in the dark inner temple, entranced, holding a laurel sprig as vapours rise around her.
ody.telem: Telemachus, the grown son of Odysseus, standing at the prow of a ship leaving Ithaca to seek news of his father, the goddess Athena beside him disguised as old Mentor.
ody.cass: Cassandra, the cursed prophetess of Troy, wild-haired and crying out her warning that no one believes, as the great wooden horse is dragged through the gates behind her.
ody.hecat: A hecatomb, the great sacrifice of a hundred oxen: altar fires burning in a row along the seashore, thick smoke rising to the gods.
ody.altar: A stone altar heaped with votive offerings, small clay figurines, garlands and burning fat, glowing in a dark sanctuary.
ody.zeus: A white marble altar of Zeus on a mountain-top at night, offering smoke rising from it, a crackling bolt of lightning striking down onto the altar from a storm-black sky.
ody.pyre: A towering funeral pyre burning on the beach at Troy at night, like the pyre of Patroclus, sparks spiralling up to the stars.
ody.ossuary: The inside of a beehive tomb like the Treasury of Atreus at Mycenae: bones, bronze helmets and grave gifts laid in the dark, a single shaft of light from the doorway.
ody.requiem: Mourners lamenting over a fallen warrior laid on a bier, arms raised in grief as on ancient Greek funeral vases, torches against a dark sky.
ody.sapper: A Trojan saboteur creeping through the night with a torch and a pick, undermining the wooden palisade of the Greek camp.
ody.salve: Asclepius, the god of healing, with his staff entwined by a single serpent, gently applying a salve to a wounded warrior's arm.
ody.gale: The bag of winds of Aeolus torn open by Odysseus's crew: a howling gale bursts from the leather sack and hurls the ship back across the wine-dark sea, away from the shores of Ithaca.
ody.hammer: Hephaestus, the lame smith god, at his forge inside a volcano, hammer raised over the anvil, sparks and molten light flying.
ody.plunder: Raiders carrying golden vessels and a bronze tripod out of a burning temple at night, the cult statue watching from the flames.
ody.thunder: Zeus hurling a jagged thunderbolt from the storm clouds, striking Odysseus's ship at sea as punishment for eating the sacred cattle of Helios.
ody.bow: The great bow of Odysseus that none of the suitors could string, drawn at last in his hall, an arrow flying through the line of twelve axe-heads.
ody.owl: The little owl of Athena with wide golden eyes, gliding on silent wings over the moonlit Acropolis.
ody.iris: Iris, goddess of the rainbow and swift messenger of the gods, with golden wings, descending along a rainbow through storm clouds.
ody.helios: Helios the sun god, crowned with rays of light, driving his blazing four-horse chariot across the sky.
ody.nike: Nike, the winged goddess of victory, swooping down over a battlefield with a laurel wreath in her hand, her robes whipping in the wind.
ody.herm: Hermes, messenger of the gods, in his winged sandals and winged cap with his herald's staff, flying swiftly over the sea with a message from Olympus.
ody.eagle: The great golden eagle of Zeus with a thunderbolt clutched in its talons, wings spread wide against storm clouds.
ody.pegasus: Pegasus, the winged white horse born from the blood of Medusa, rearing in flight above the clouds at dawn.
ody.mino: The Minotaur, the bull-headed son of the Cretan queen, in the dark stone corridors of the Labyrinth at Knossos, torchlight and bones on the floor.
ody.cerb: Cerberus, the colossal three-headed hound of Hades, with a serpent for a tail and snakes along his back, snarling with glowing ember eyes at the gates of the underworld, the river Styx and green-black mist behind.
ody.tbull: The great white bull that Poseidon sent from the sea to King Minos, rising out of the waves onto the shore of Crete.
ody.charon: Charon, the grim old ferryman of the dead, poling his boat across the dark river Styx, pale shades waiting on the bank, a coin for the fare in his outstretched hand.
ody.capt: A veteran hoplite captain in a tall horsehair-crested helmet pointing his sword forward, ordering his shield line to advance.
ody.bastion: Spartan warriors in red cloaks standing shoulder to shoulder as a living wall before unwalled Sparta, because its men were its walls, Mount Taygetus behind.
ody.sack: Odysseus's men sacking and burning Ismarus, city of the Cicones, at night, the first raid on the voyage home from Troy.
ody.dio2: Diomedes the Bold driving his spear at the war god Ares himself with Athena's help, fire blazing from his helmet as the Iliad describes.
ody.muse: A Muse playing a lyre by a spring on Mount Helicon under the stars, a young poet listening, entranced.
ody.peltast: A light-armed Greek skirmisher with a crescent-shaped wicker shield, running and hurling a javelin.
ody.medic: Machaon, son of Asclepius and surgeon of the Greek army at Troy, binding a wounded warrior's leg inside a lamp-lit tent.
ody.pikeman: A guard of the Taphians, the sea-raiding people of the Odyssey, with a long pike and a hide shield, standing watch over a rocky harbour.
ody.veteran: A grey-bearded Athenian hoplite with old scars, standing on the marshy plain of Marathon, the burial mound of the fallen behind him.
ody.corsair: A Cicone raider from Thrace leaping from a small boat onto a beach, blade raised, painted shield on his arm.
ody.harrier: A raider blowing a horn from the prow of a ship as a pack of boats rushes into a harbour town at dawn.
ody.reaver: A hooded assassin in shadow dipping arrowheads into poison from a small clay pot, like the arrow-poison Odysseus sought at Ephyra.
ody.ram: Warriors under a wooden roof swinging a bronze-headed battering ram against a great city gate, splinters flying.
ody.augur: A seer like Calchas reading the flight of birds against a stormy sky, arms raised, the Greek fleet waiting below.
ody.sphinx: The Sphinx of Thebes, with a woman's face, a lion's body and an eagle's wings, perched on a rock outside the city to pose her riddle, bones scattered below.
ody.karma: The three Fates in a dark cave: one spinning the thread of life, one measuring it, one about to cut it with shears.
ody.leon: Leonidas, King of Sparta, a bearded warrior-king in a red cloak and a crested bronze helmet, holding a large round bronze shield, standing calm and proud in the narrow mountain pass of Thermopylae, warm sunset light on the cliffs behind him.
ody.thermo: The narrow pass of Thermopylae between cliffs and the sea, a small line of Greek shields facing an endless Persian host at sunset.
ody.brasidas: Brasidas, the bold Spartan general, leading his men on a night march through the mountains of Thrace, red cloak and crested helmet in moonlight.
ody.pent: Penthesilea, queen of the Amazons, charging into battle at Troy on horseback with a double-headed axe and a crescent shield.
ody.horde: A mounted charge of Amazon warriors across a plain, axes and spears raised, horses at full gallop in a storm of dust.
ody.eury: Eurylochus, Odysseus's kinsman and second-in-command, a hard bearded sailor-warrior leading the crew ashore on Circe's island with a drawn sword, wary of the forest.
ody.iph: Iphigenia, daughter of Agamemnon, standing calmly at the altar at Aulis in a white robe as the goddess Artemis spirits her away and a deer appears in her place in a burst of light, the becalmed fleet behind.
ody.hades: Hades, Lord of the Dead, enthroned in the dark underworld with a dark crown and two-pronged staff, Cerberus at his feet, pale shades drifting in the distance.
ody.thanat: Thanatos, the winged god of death, a solemn dark-winged young man holding an upside-down extinguished torch, gliding silently over a battlefield at dusk.
ody.games: The funeral games for Patroclus at Troy: chariots racing around a turning post, the burial mound behind, crowds of warriors cheering.
